questions.question: How do you want to handle the DSTrader.jar history blob before the first 6a mirror push?

options.label: Defer to #19 (HUMAN-ONLY filter-repo)
options.description: You do the filter-repo cleanup of audit residuals (jar blob + anything else #7 left behind) per the existing #19 scope, push the rewritten history to dstrader (or a new repo per the rollback-acceptable memory), then I re-run the SOP audit. Matches existing ticket scope; agents don't touch history.

options.label: Manager-dispatched scrub to new repo
options.description: I dispatch a worker to run `git filter-repo --strip-blobs-bigger-than 1M` against a fresh clone, push to a NEW private repo (e.g. dstrader-rewritten), preserving current `dstrader` untouched. Mirrors what the FF manager is doing for FamilyFund. You'd authorize the new-repo creation + push in the moment. Absorbs #19 into one mechanical action.

options.label: Ship as-is
options.description: Accept the residual risk. Strict gitleaks is clean; jar contents are derived from source that's going public anyway; rollback-acceptable memory applies if something surfaces post-publish. Closes #19 as wontfix or rescopes it. Fastest path to first sync.

options.label: Pause — want to inspect the jar first
options.description: Hold the decision while you (or I) extract the jar from history and grep its contents for paths/usernames to inform the call. Adds a step but de-risks the Ship-as-is option.

## Worker reply triaged — FINDINGS, one decision point

**Mechanically clean:** strict gitleaks HEAD=0/ALL=0, all Step-2 greps explainable (46 IB hits all synthetic `U0000003-5`/`DU0000001-2`; 3 envlike all shell-var FPs), 0 workflow secrets (security-scan.yml only, default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no fork-exfil), files-suspicious empty.

**The single finding:** `DSTrader.jar` (~MB Java build artefact) reachable from `main` history. Removed at HEAD by `850e5c2` (#4), `*.jar` is now gitignored, so no recurrence. But under the adopted **6a mirror push**, all history goes to `dstrader-public` — the blob would be retrievable via `git cat-file` from the public repo, not in the public HEAD tree.

**Why this is non-trivial despite "gitleaks-clean":** strict gitleaks treats the blob as binary and doesn't text-scan it. A jar built from pre-sanitization source can carry, inside compiled class files / SourceFile attributes / embedded resources, content that the Step-2 tree grep cannot see — e.g. pre-#2 `/Users/dtogni/...` paths embedded in debug info, or pre-#3 string literals if the build pre-dated those scrubs. Strict gitleaks's clean verdict doesn't dismiss this risk; it just confirms no signature-rule hit.

**This is exactly the scope of existing ticket dstrader#1 / #19** — "HUMAN-ONLY follow-up to #7: filter-repo cleanup of audit residuals." The jar blob is an audit residual.
Understood — deferring to #19. Archiving the worker, updating the board.
